thread:
incident-bot: SEV1 ALERT: gateway-prod elevated 5xx rate >3% for 5m, increased timeouts. paging oncall. grafana: https://grafana.redwood.example/d/abcd/gateway-prod?orgId=1

marie: @raj paging you, you're oncall for US region. :ambulance:

raj: on it. seeing spike in gateway 5xx and gateway_timeouts. which pool is backing this?

alex: looks like batching/scheduler queues in us-west are saturated. batcher.queue_length{pool=\"encoder\"} ~ 5k, head-of-line blocking on a few client streams. p95 token latency climbing.

raj: pulling logs from batcher pods now 
```bash
kubectl -n runtime logs -l app=batcher -c worker --tail=200 | grep -E \"enqueue|evict|timeout\"
```

ops-bot: Autoscaler attempted to add nodes but provision time >2m; allocation pending due to capacity constraints in region-us-west. KV cache warmup observed; long-lived KV entries preventing efficient batching.

raj: quick mitigation proposal: 1) reduce batch_size on encoder pool from 32 -> 8, 2) enable aggressive preemptive eviction for requests >120s, 3) route high-priority traffic to fallback fast-quantized variant. Can apply now?

marie: +1, do it. Notify support/CS.

raj: applying config change to pool encoder: 
```yaml
pool: encoder
batch_size: 8
eviction_policy: aggressive
preempt_timeout_s: 120
```
Applying...
```
raj: config rolled out to 3/3 pool instances.

marie: monitoring metrics... p50 improved almost immediately, p95 still elevated for a subset. 5xx count trending down but not back to baseline. :eyes: 

raj: digging into logs found multiple very long requests from a single client id (client_7x) that hold KV cache entries and prevent batching across others — classic head-of-line.

alex: can we cancel or isolate that client's inflight work? The runtime exposes per-client queue caps now, but we haven't enabled them. We can add a temporary routing rule to send client_7x to a dedicated pool with batch_size=1.

ops-bot: applying routing rule: 
```
route: client_7x -> pool=encoder-isolated batch_size=1
```

ops-bot: route applied. new pod pool provisioning in progress (2 pods requested).

support-sally: support update: 7 customer tickets opened reporting 500s and some timeouts. CS notified for enterprise accounts. Draft status page message ready for approval.

marie: approved. post status: Investigating — elevated error rates and timeouts for some customers in US-WEST. Working on mitigation; updates every 15m.

raj: rolling restart one batcher pod to clear stuck KV state (graceful). 
```bash
kubectl -n runtime rollout restart deployment/batcher-encoder-2
```
raj: pod batcher-encoder-2 restarted and rejoined cluster. queues decreased ~40%.

alex: after routing client_7x and restarts, 5xx dropped to near baseline. remaining errors look like downstream gateway timeouts (504) from long-run requests.

marie: current status: error rate down from peak 3.8% -> 0.6% over 15m. p95 latency improved but a tail remains for a small cohort. No broad data loss or auth issues observed.

raj: plan for next 12h: 1) keep eviction aggressive, 2) enforce per-client queue cap 50, 3) add early-reject for requests exceeding 30s token-processing, 4) schedule postmortem to root cause KV growth.

alex: initial hypothesis: a long-context client producing very large KV footprint + autoscaler lag causing HOL blocking and batcher saturation. Recommend follow-ups: model-level chunking, per-client quotas, and quicker cache eviction heuristics.

support-sally: I notified the three affected enterprise accounts and created ticket ENG-INC-9472. CS will follow up with timeline and mitigation steps.

marie: thanks. any customer visible action needed from us besides status updates?

support-sally: customers asked for ETA for full recovery; we should say investigating with mitigations in place, monitoring.

ops-bot: autoscaler now provisioned the two isolate pods; encoding pool capacity up +2.

raj: handing off to alex for deeper debug and postmortem ownership. I'm stepping off in 25m. jordan will be next oncall.

alex: taking over. I will collect heap/KV metrics, sample offending requests (sanitized), and open a follow-up RFC for per-client caps.

oncall-bot: Handoff: raj -> alex (active), next oncall: jordan (starts rotation in 25m). Include timeline and actions: reduced batch_size, eviction=aggressive, client_7x routed to isolated pool, 3 pod restarts, status page updated, CS briefed.

marie: thanks team. will create incident ticket with mitigation timeline and link to logs/dashboards. Postmortem owners: alex (lead), raj (backup), timeline due EOD.

incident-bot: INCIDENT MITIGATED (SEV1->DEGRADED). Continue monitoring.

jordan: ACKED, I'll join the follow-up and keep an eye on the tail latency.

marie: closing channel for now — move follow-ups to #postmortems and #eng-runtime.
